title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey, October 2026 — the first regional Fed prices-paid read of the month
source: EST: newyorkfed.org/survey/empire/empiresurvey_overview — the New York Fed's own survey overview page, fetched direct 2026-09-08 by the cpi-2026-10-14 D-36 pulse-check adjacency sweep. Its release calendar lists the 2026 dates month by month — Jan 15, Feb 17, Mar 16, Apr 15, May 15, Jun 15, Jul 15, Aug 17 as released, then Sep 15, OCT 15, Nov 16, Dec 15 forward — and states the timing verbatim: 'Released at or shortly after 8:30 a.m.' The month-by-month pattern is internally consistent (the 15th, rolled to the next business day when the 15th is a weekend: Feb 15 2026 was a Sunday and the page shows Feb 17; Aug 15 was a Saturday and the page shows Aug 17; Oct 15 2026 is a Thursday, so no roll applies). Filed estimate on two counts, neither of which is doubt about the date: this calendar's confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (there is FED: for the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the same two reasons eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17 was filed estimate off its publisher's own primary. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the cpi-2026-10-14 D-36 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08). It earns a row for a coverage gap in the 10-14 corridor, not for a price channel. That corridor grew from 2 tracked ids at D-44 to 17 today, and it is now three prints deep on 10-15 alone (PPI, retail sales, Treasury coupon announcement) — but this calendar tracks ZERO regional Federal Reserve manufacturing surveys for October, despite carrying chicago-pmi and dallas-fed-mfg entries for other months. Empire State is the FIRST regional Fed survey of each month and the earliest read on the month currently underway, and its prices-paid / prices-received components are a same-cycle inflation signal published the morning AFTER the September-data CPI. Why that ordering matters for the sweep that found it: cpi-2026-10-14 publishes September data on 10-14, and Empire State publishes OCTOBER survey responses on 10-15 — so the pair reads as a backward-looking official number followed within 24 hours by a forward-looking business survey covering the month the official number does not yet touch. In an energy shock whose pass-through into goods prices is the live question (US regular gasoline $4.071/gal week ending 2026-08-31 vs $3.177 a year ago, EIA primary; AAA daily $4.15 on 09-04, a September record), the prices-paid line is where that pass-through shows up first. Impact LOW and symbols empty, deliberately: no house playbook is keyed to regional surveys, none of the nine tracked names carries a New-York-district manufacturing channel, and Empire State's own headline index is famously noisy month to month — what the entry buys is that the next inflation sweep sees it on the calendar instead of missing it, and that the 10-15 stack is honestly counted at four prints rather than three. Read limits, stated so it is not overread later: a district survey is a diffusion index over roughly 100 respondents, not a price level, so it can never confirm or refute a CPI print; and this entry is an ESTIMATE, which widens caution and licenses nothing.
